items.answer: With independent genes: uniform crossover is better because it treats all positions equally and has higher mixing rate (50% chance per gene from each parent), leading to faster building block assembly. With strong linkage between adjacent genes: single-point crossover preserves building blocks better since it swaps contiguous segments, reducing disruption of co-adapted gene complexes. Two-point crossover is a compromise.

items.answer: High selection pressure (e.g., rank-based or truncation selection) drives the population toward the nearest peak quickly. Once most individuals cluster around x=3, crossover between similar parents rarely produces offspring near x=7. The valley at x=5 has low fitness so migrants are selected against. Modifications: (1) adaptive mutation rate that increases when diversity drops, (2) island model with periodic migration, (3) niching/crowding to maintain diversity, (4) simulated annealing-style acceptance of worse solutions early on.
